summary: Lincoln County, NM lookout (register: built 1931) where the May 1950 fire was first spotted; removed for a prehistoric pueblo, date not found; no current site description found.

facts.status_note: Register says it was removed in favor of preserving a prehistoric pueblo; no removal date in the sources read; no description of the site today found

staffing.status: summertime fire lookout for 25 years; retiring in August 1957 (1957 newspaper item)

events.note: Register 'Built' field gives 1931 for a ground house-type lookout; no second source gives a build date
May 1950 fire of about 14,000 acres on the Capitan Ranger District; first spotted from the lookout; a burned cub was rescued from it
Mr. Latham, called Bob in the same item, had served 25 years as summertime lookout at Block; retiring August 1957
Forest Service announced Block Lookout would become Smokey Bear Lookout (item dated December 24, 1959); the sources do not confirm the change was applied
Registered August 30, 2015 as FFLOS US 1605, NM 4

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1931 with no second source. A 1957 item refers to an older station and to 'the present tower' but gives no build date. The story gives the register's date and says it rests on the register alone.

notes_for_editor: Build date (1931) comes only from the register. The 1957 item's wording implies an older station, so check Lincoln NF or New Mexico records before relying on it. Removal date not found; the Forest Lookouts 'Removed' heading has no details. No source found on the site today or on public access. The 1959 item reports an announced rename only; the register lists both names. The register's 'Administered by' field reads 'U.s. Forest Service' (casing as printed), which matches the 1959 item; this JSON uses the standard 'U.S.' spelling. The story does not name the agency. Two search results (a tribal fire crew article and Monjeau Lookout) were not used.
